sampling_model.design: Independent sampling of complete recorded trajectories from a finite-horizon behavior process.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent trajectories with one multinomial cell in \(\mathcal O\) per trajectory.
sampling_model.treatment: Actions are generated by the known recorded-history behavior policy \(\mu\). The fixed deployment rule \(\pi\) is an oracle complete-information policy when it uses latent rewards; deployment requires a separately supplied reward-recovery or sensing mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: \(\mu_t(a\mid H_t^O)\ge\epsilon>0\) on every finite history-action cell.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The observed multinomial law is inverted jointly for validity. Fixed-law value images are computed by exact real quantifier elimination over latent trajectory probabilities; the KL confidence fiber is not represented as a polynomial program.

body.tldr: Finite-horizon off-policy value with MNAR discrete rewards is the image of a compact semialgebraic full-history fiber. The sole headline target is an exact \(H=2\), binary-action, three-reward generic strict-containment result: a coefficient-complete observed table, rational completion parameterization, observable elimination minors with a nonempty relatively open sign region, an exact witness, and the exceptional equality variety. A compact common-face lemma is supporting geometry, and the one-stage Chen reduction is a non-novel sanity proposition anchored only by the source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\). Sharp endpoint attainment and fixed-law exact elimination remain supporting results.

project_justification.gap: Static weak-shadow linear programs do not characterize dynamic compatibility when latent reward completion changes later oracle-policy occupancy. Iyengar's rectangular robust dynamic program assumes the product structure that an MNAR observed-data inverse fiber need not possess.
project_justification.niche: The missing theorem-level object is a checkable, coefficient-complete, relatively open region on which the exact two-stage inverse fiber has a strict endpoint gap from its stagewise product-of-projections relaxation.
project_justification.fill: The project makes that exact two-stage generic strict-containment dossier the sole headline obligation. Compact attainment, common-face geometry, the source-label-pinned one-stage Chen sanity reduction, and fixed-law quantifier elimination serve only as supporting results.

body.related_work: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong (2026), in the source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' use the program at equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\) and the full-column-rank conclusion at proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\). In the one-stage sanity proposition, \(S_2\) plays their always-observed \(F\) role; no static novelty is claimed. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, obtains robust Bellman recursion under rectangular ambiguity, whereas the headline obligation must prove that the present inverse observed-data fiber is strictly nonrectangular on a relatively open set. Wang, Xu, Lu, and Song (2025) identify and estimate MNAR OPE values through a response model and inverse weighting. Wei, Qu, and Miao (2026) use a current-state exclusion, bridge conditions, and completeness to point identify finite-horizon value. Their current-state exclusion neither implies nor is implied by \(S_{t+1}\perp M_t\mid(H_t^F,A_t,R_t)\) without additional Markov or sufficiency conditions. Duarte et al. (2024) inform certified optimization for finite discrete causal models. Chen, Christensen, and Tamer (2018) inform set-level inversion. Bennett et al. (2026) and Li, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023) study functionals under nuisance nonuniqueness, but their static operator arguments do not address latent-history-dependent continuation occupancy.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Generic strict containment is not asserted until the single open obligation prints the entire two-stage rational table, affine completion map, coefficient-expanded minors, strict sign region, exact witness, and exceptional equality variety. The maintained exclusion fails when recording changes subsequent care or shares residual causes with next-state innovation. A complete-information policy is operationally unavailable without a reward-recovery or sensing mechanism. The identified value image need not be an interval because the weak-shadow fiber can be nonconvex, so fixed-law computation retains every connected component. The exact multinomial confidence fiber is not claimed to have a polynomial encoding.
body.honest_scope: Compactness, endpoint attainment, the supporting compact-face identity, and fixed-law real quantifier elimination have direct proof routes. The sole headline is the exact \(H=2\) generic strict-containment open obligation; the required coefficient-complete table, observable sign certificate, relatively open region, exact witness, and equality variety are not treated as established. The one-stage proposition is only a sanity reduction to Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong's source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\), with \(S_2\) in the always-observed \(F\) role and explicit response positivity. Iyengar's Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, is a comparator that assumes rectangular ambiguity; it does not prove rectangularity for an inverse observed-data fiber. The full-history exclusion is maintained rather than inherited from either static Chen conditions or Wei, Qu, and Miao's current-state exclusion. A latent-reward-dependent \(\pi\) is an oracle target unless implementation is separately supplied.
